turns.ask: Our online game's login API keeps getting hammered by massive DDoS attacks. Design the full protection layer and the backend service behind it.

ops.text: I'll design a DDoS-hardened login API path: Anti-DDoS Proxy, WAF on the ALB, and backend game services in Singapore.
Protect game login API from massive DDoS attacks

ops.label: Game players
ops.why: Players calling the login API from devices worldwide.

ops.label: Cloud DNS
ops.why: Resolves the login domain to Anti-DDoS Proxy CNAME.

ops.label: Anti-DDoS Proxy
ops.why: Scrubbing center absorbs volumetric L3-L7 DDoS before origin.

ops.label: ALB
ops.why: Layer-7 load balancer distributing scrubbed login traffic.

ops.label: WAF 3.0
ops.why: Blocks CC floods, bot abuse and OWASP attacks on login.

ops.label: API Gateway
ops.why: Rate limits, auth checks and routing for the login API.

ops.text: Backend runs on ECS with Auto Scaling, sessions in Tair, accounts in RDS.

ops.label: Login servers
ops.why: Stateless login microservice validating credentials.

ops.label: Auto Scaling
ops.why: Scales login servers during attack-surviving traffic spikes.

ops.label: Session cache
ops.why: Stores tokens and rate-limit counters in memory.

ops.label: Accounts DB
ops.why: Persistent player account store with HA standby.

ops.label: NAT Gateway
ops.why: Outbound internet for patching without exposing login servers.

ops.label: Log Service
ops.why: Centralizes access logs, WAF events and login audit trail.

ops.label: CloudMonitor
ops.why: Alarms on DDoS volume, latency and error rates.
